profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company, traded as CRNC and headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, that describes itself as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond. Its work is powered by CaLLM, which the company describes as its family of language models, and it says it is moving to advance generative AI and LLM-powered innovation it expects to be central to the automotive and transportation user experience. The company says it builds tailor-made AI solutions that integrate with vehicle makers' own systems while preserving their brand identity.

Among the products described on its site is Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection, or EVD, which the company says is already deployed in production vehicles. Cerence says EVD uses existing vehicle microphones and AI trained to distinguish sirens from traffic, road noise, music and other sounds, and can detect and localize more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, identifying approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters with exterior microphones. The site also describes dynamic speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments, allowing passengers in different zones to make requests at once, and a demonstration of that work is credited to Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich. A piece on Zero Trust Architecture for in-car assistants is credited to Kaivan Karimi, described as Business Development Senior Director at Cerence AI, and Frank Kaleck, described as Director Industry Advisory Automotive at Microsoft, and the site describes Cerence AI and Microsoft using Zero Trust and layered AI security to protect in-car assistants. In its third quarter results, the company reported revenue up 12% YoY, connected services revenue up 20% YoY, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting its first-ever share repurchase program.

Corporate records list the company under CIK 0001768267. Its recorded litigation exposure is in Massachusetts, where 126 cases are counted.
